mainTopic: Oil and the קומץ, רבא's unresolved question about oil on the altar wood, a משנה on mixed מנחות, and רב חסדא and רבי חנינא on cancelling נבילה and שחוטה.
overview: First, רבא explains רבי יהודה's rule for mixtures. You set aside the same kind as if it were not there, and a larger amount of a different kind cancels it out. Next, רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about a קומץ of a מנחת חוטא that got oil on it. רבי יוחנן says it is פסול, and ריש לקיש says it is fine. ריש לקיש survives a challenge from a פסוק and two challenges from ברייתות. Then רבא asks whether oil squeezed onto the altar wood still counts as part of the קומץ. רבינא links this question to the bone-and-limb dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. רב אשי shows that the cases may be different, so the question ends as תיקו. A new משנה then teaches what happens when מנחות or a קומץ get mixed together. In the גמרא, רב חסדא and רבי חנינא give opposite rules about when נבילה and שחוטה cancel each other in a mixture. The גמרא asks which earlier opinion they follow, and it shows they cannot follow the רבנן. It then starts testing רבי יהודה, a challenge that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: רבא explains רבי יהודה's rule for mixtures
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי יהודה ignores the same kind in a mixture, and lets the different kind cancel it out if the different kind is larger.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי יהודה holds that whenever something is mixed with its own kind and also with a different kind, you treat its own kind as if it is not there. Then, if the different kind is more than it, the different kind cancels it out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the reasoning behind רבי יהודה's view about a mixture. The mixture has both 'the same kind' and 'a different kind' in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the same kind cannot cancel out the same kind. רבי יהודה says to ignore the same kind and look only at the different kind. If the different kind is larger, it cancels out the smaller one. Here, the foreign oil is cancelled into the larger flour of the קומץ, so it counts as the קומץ's own oil. That gives the קומץ too much oil.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this is his reasoning)
A substance mixed with its own kind
A different substance
Is more than it and cancels it out (ביטול)

steps.confusionAlert: The 'different kind' is not being cancelled here; it is the one doing the cancelling. It can do that only because the same kind is set aside as if it were not there.

phrases.english: Rava said: Rabbi Yehuda holds,
any case of a substance with its own kind
and also another substance:
remove its own kind as if it were not there,
phrases.notes: In our case, the oil of the handful is 'its own kind' next to the other offering's oil, so it gets set aside.

phrases.english: and what is not its kind is more than it and cancels it out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי יהודה's position from the earlier discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, in a mixture of the same kind plus a different kind, ignore the same kind; the larger different kind cancels it out.

steps.title: Dispute: a sinner's handful that got oil on it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says a קומץ of a מנחת חוטא that got oil on it is פסול. ריש לקיש says one even wipes it in leftover oil and then offers it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if someone put oil on the handful of a sinner's meal offering, רבי יוחנן says it is unfit. ריש לקיש says that one even wipes it on purpose in the leftover oil of the log and then brings it up on the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: an argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about a מנחת חוטא's קומץ that got oil on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנחת חוטא is supposed to have no oil at all. רבי יוחנן says any oil ruins it. ריש לקיש says a little oil does not ruin it. In fact, one even wipes the קומץ in the leftover oil from earlier offerings before burning it.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful of flour the כהן takes from a meal offering to burn on the מזבח
A sinner's meal offering, brought by a poor person, with no oil or frankincense
Unfit, cannot be offered
He wipes it or rubs it around
The leftover oil of the לוג measure, from earlier offerings

steps.whyThisMatters: This argument is the base for the challenges in the rest of the section.

phrases.english: It was stated: a handful of a sinner's meal offering that one put oil on,
Rabbi Yochanan says: it is unfit,
and Reish Lakish said:
one even wipes it on purpose
in the leftovers of the log of oil, and brings it up on the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related topic about oil and the קומץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: a קומץ of a מנחת חוטא with oil on it is פסול. ריש לקיש: it is fine, and one even wipes it in leftover oil.

steps.title: A verse says no oil on a sinner's offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש from the פסוק that forbids putting oil on a מנחת חוטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written: 'He shall not put oil on it, and he shall not put frankincense on it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks ריש לקיש's view with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says clearly not to put oil on a מנחת חוטא. So how can ריש לקיש allow wiping it in oil on purpose?

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (a challenge from a פסוק)
Frankincense

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"He shall not put oil on it
and he shall not put frankincense on it"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's view from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's ruling that one may wipe the קומץ of a מנחת חוטא in oil
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק forbids putting oil on a מנחת חוטא, which seems to contradict adding oil on purpose.

steps.title: The verse only forbids a set portion of oil
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק only means not to set aside a full measure of oil for it like other מנחות have.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse means that one should not set aside oil for it the way one does for the other meal offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and defends ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is read narrowly. It forbids giving the מנחת חוטא its own set portion of oil, like other מנחות get. A little leftover oil wiped on it is not what the פסוק forbids.

keyTerms.meaning: Set aside as a fixed portion
Like its fellows, meaning the other meal offerings

phrases.english: That verse means he should not set aside oil for it
like its fellow meal offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא שֶׁלֹּא יִקְבַּע לָהּ שֶׁמֶן כְּחַבְרוֹתֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the meaning of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק forbids any oil at all on a מנחת חוטא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק only forbids a set portion of oil, like other מנחות have. A little leftover oil is allowed.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן challenges from a dry offering mixed with an oily one
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה says a dry מנחה mixed with an oily one may not be offered. He suggests this means a מנחת חוטא's קומץ mixed with a נדבה's קומץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש: A dry meal offering that got mixed with one mixed with oil may be offered. רבי יהודה says it may not be offered. Isn't this talking about the handful of a sinner's meal offering that got mixed with the handful of a voluntary meal offering?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from a ברייתא. He suggests a reading that would show oil does ruin a מנחת חוטא's קומץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'dry' offering is understood as a מנחת חוטא, and the 'oily' one as a מנחת נדבה. רבי יהודה says not to offer the mixture. That would show that oil touching the sinner's קומץ makes it unfit, which goes against ריש לקיש. The words 'מאי לאו' show this is a suggested reading, not yet proven.

keyTerms.meaning: Dry, meaning a meal offering with no oil
Mixed with oil
A voluntary meal offering, which has oil
Isn't it…? (introduces a suggested reading)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan raised a challenge to Reish Lakish:
a dry meal offering that got mixed with one mixed with oil:
he shall offer it,
Rabbi Yehuda says: he shall not offer it.
Isn't it talking about a handful of a sinner's meal offering
that got mixed with a handful of a voluntary meal offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the פסוק challenge was answered, רבי יוחנן brings a new challenge from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's ruling that oil does not make a מנחת חוטא's קומץ unfit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא is about a מנחת חוטא's קומץ mixed with an oily נדבה קומץ, then רבי יהודה's 'do not offer' shows that oil makes the sinner's קומץ unfit.

steps.title: ריש לקיש reads the ברייתא as bull and ram offerings mixed with sheep offerings
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that 'dry mixed with oily' means the מנחה of bulls and rams mixed with the מנחה of sheep, not a מנחת חוטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means the מנחה that comes with bulls and rams that got mixed with the מנחה that comes with sheep.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש pushes back on רבי יוחנן's proof. He says the ברייתא is talking about a different case, not a מנחת חוטא at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנחה that comes with bulls and rams has less oil for each measure of flour than the מנחה that comes with sheep. So next to the sheep's מנחה it counts as 'dry.' With this reading, רבי יהודה says nothing about an oily קומץ of a מנחת חוטא, and ריש לקיש's view is safe.

keyTerms.meaning: The flour offering that comes along with an animal קרבן
Bulls and rams
Sheep (lambs)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Dry' here does not mean it has no oil at all. It only means it has less oil than the sheep's מנחה it got mixed with.

phrases.english: No, [it means] the meal offering of bulls and rams
phrases.notes: The 'dry' one here has less oil for each measure of flour than the sheep's offering.

phrases.english: [mixed] with the meal offering of sheep.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא, מִנְחַת פָּרִים וְאֵילִים בְּמִנְחַת כְּבָשִׂים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's challenge from the ברייתא by giving it a different case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Dry mixed with oily' means a מנחת חוטא's קומץ mixed with a נדבה's קומץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means a bull or ram מנחת נסכים mixed with a sheep מנחת נסכים.

steps.title: Another ברייתא lists the bull and ram case separately
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן shows a ברייתא that names the bull and ram case and also names 'dry mixed with oily' as a second case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches this case openly: the מנחה of bulls and rams mixed with the מנחה of sheep, and a dry one mixed with an oily one, may be offered. רבי יהודה says it may not be offered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks ריש לקיש's reading. Another ברייתא lists the bull and ram case by name and then adds 'dry mixed with oily' as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'dry mixed with oily' only meant bulls and rams mixed with sheep, the ברייתא would be saying the same thing twice. So the 'dry mixed with oily' case must be about something else, like a מנחת חוטא. That brings back the problem for ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Openly, in so many words
It may be offered

phrases.english: But it teaches this explicitly:
The meal offering of bulls and rams [mixed] with the meal offering of sheep,
and a dry one that got mixed with an oil-mixed one, may be offered;
Rabbi Yehuda says: It may not be offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's reinterpretation from Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that 'dry mixed with oily' means bulls and rams mixed with sheep
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists both cases one after the other. That suggests they are two different cases, so 'dry mixed with oily' cannot just mean the bull and ram case.

steps.title: The second clause explains the first
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that 'dry mixed with oily' is not a new case. It explains why the bull and ram case is a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is explaining it.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש defends himself. The words 'dry mixed with oily' are not a second case; they explain the first case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read the ברייתא this way: the bull and ram מנחה mixed with the sheep מנחה, meaning a dry one mixed with an oily one. So רבי יהודה forbids it because it is dry mixed with oily. The ברייתא does not mention a מנחת חוטא at all.

keyTerms.meaning: It is explaining it (the second clause explains the first)

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's view survives. Every ברייתא about 'dry mixed with oily' can be read as the bull and ram מנחה mixed with the sheep מנחה, not a מנחת חוטא.

phrases.english: It is explaining it.
phrases.notes: The words 'dry mixed with oily' tell us why the bull and ram case is a problem. They are not a separate case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's objection in Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording: the second clause explains the first
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lists two separate cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is one case. The second clause gives the reason for the first.

steps.title: רבא asks about a קומץ whose oil was squeezed onto the wood
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether oil that soaked into the altar wood still counts as part of the קומץ that is burned on top of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: A קומץ whose oil was squeezed out onto the wood, what is the law? Is something attached to what goes up on the altar treated like what goes up, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבא asks a question about a קומץ whose oil was squeezed out onto the altar wood before the קומץ itself was put there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oil is now in the wood, and the קומץ is burned on top of it. The question is whether something touching or attached to the קרבן counts as part of what is offered. If it does, the קומץ has its oil. If not, the קומץ is missing its oil.

keyTerms.meaning: He asks a question that has no clear answer yet
The handful of flour taken from a מנחה and burned on the altar
Squeezed out
Things attached to what goes up on the altar
Are treated like the things that go up

phrases.english: Rava asked:
A handful whose oil he squeezed out
onto the wood, what is the law?
Are things attached to what goes up treated like what goes up,
or are they not treated like what goes up?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about oil and the קומץ, after the earlier discussion of oil on a קומץ.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does oil absorbed into the altar wood count as part of the קומץ burned on it?

steps.title: רבינא links רבא's question to a known מחלוקת
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי whether רבא's question is the same as a known disagreement between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Isn't this the same as the disagreement of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא suggests that רבא's question is not new. It may already be the subject of a known מחלוקת. This line sets up the source he is about to quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an earlier dispute is about the same idea, whether attached things count as part of the קרבן, then רבא's question depends on that dispute. רבינא is about to show which dispute he means.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't this the same as

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: לָאו הַיְינוּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ?
phrases.english: Isn't this the same as [the dispute of] Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו הַיְינוּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests that רבא's question in Step 9 is the same as an existing מחלוקת.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's question about oil attached to the קומץ
steps.raayaSupportSource: The מחלוקת of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, quoted in the next step

steps.title: The dispute about a limb completed to a כזית by its bone
steps.stepSummary: Someone offers outside the בית המקדש a limb with less than a כזית of meat, and the bone brings it up to a כזית. רבי יוחנן says he is liable; ריש לקיש says he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was said: If someone offers up a limb that does not have a כזית of meat, and the bone completes it to a כזית, רבי יוחנן says he is liable and ריש לקיש says he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the source רבינא had in mind. It is a disagreement about whether the bone, which is attached to the meat, counts toward the כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן counts the attached bone toward the כזית, so the person is liable. That is like saying attached things count as part of what goes up. ריש לקיש does not count the bone, so the person is exempt. רבינא's point is that this matches the two sides of רבא's question.

keyTerms.meaning: One who offers up (here, outside the בית המקדש)
A limb of an animal
An olive-sized amount, the smallest amount that counts
Bone
Liable / exempt

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבא's question may depend on a basic מחלוקת: does something attached to a קרבן count as part of it?

phrases.english: As it was stated:
One who offers up a limb that does not contain an olive-bulk,
phrases.notes: He means offering it outside the בית המקדש, which is forbidden.

phrases.english: and the bone completes it to an olive-bulk:
Rabbi Yochanan says: He is liable;
Reish Lakish says: He is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִיתְּמַר: הַמַּעֲלֶה אֵבֶר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ כְּזַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the dispute that רבינא pointed to in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A limb with less than a כזית that its bone completes: רבי יוחנן says liable, ריש לקיש says exempt.

steps.title: The reasons behind the bone dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says liable because things attached to the burned parts count like them. ריש לקיש says exempt because they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says he is liable, because things attached to what goes up on the מזבח are treated like what goes up. ריש לקיש says he is exempt, because things attached to what goes up are not treated like what goes up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind each side of the dispute from the last step about the limb with a bone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole argument is about one idea: does the bone, which is attached to the meat, join the meat to make a כזית? רבי יוחנן says yes, so the person is liable. ריש לקיש says no, so there is less than a כזית and he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Things attached to the parts that go up on the מזבח
They are treated like the parts that go up
Liable (he is punished)
Exempt (not punished)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: attached things count (חיבורי עולין כעולין דמו). ריש לקיש: attached things do not count.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: he is liable,
things attached to what goes up are like what goes up,
phrases.notes: "What goes up" means the parts burned on the מזבח. Here, the bone is attached to the meat.

phrases.english: and Reish Lakish says: he is exempt,
things attached to what goes up are not like what goes up.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר חַיָּיב, חִיבּוּרֵי עוֹלִין כְּעוֹלִין דָּמוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasons for the rulings stated in step 11, which רבינא suggested match רבא's question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: attached parts count like the burned parts. ריש לקיש: they do not.

steps.title: The question still stands for רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that רבא's question can be asked on both sides. Even רבי יוחנן might only count the bone, because it is the same kind as the meat, but not oil, which is a different kind than the קומץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: The question can be asked according to רבי יוחנן, and it can be asked according to ריש לקיש. According to רבי יוחנן: he only said his rule there, about a bone, because a bone is the same kind as meat. But oil, which is not the same kind as the קומץ, does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects רבינא's idea that רבא's question is the same as the bone dispute, and starts showing why with רבי יוחנן's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא thought that whoever counts the bone would also count the soaked oil. רב אשי points out a difference: the bone comes from the same animal as the meat, but oil is a different kind of thing than the flour of the קומץ. So even רבי יוחנן might say the oil does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: The question can still be asked
He only said it in this case and no further
The same kind or type
The handful taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying רבי יוחנן holds the oil does not count. He is only saying it might be so, so the bone dispute does not answer רבא's question.

phrases.english: The question can be asked according to Rabbi Yochanan,
and the question can be asked according to Reish Lakish.
It can be asked according to Rabbi Yochanan:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָתָם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan only said his rule there,
in the case of a bone, because it is the same kind as the meat,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הַאי דְּלָאו דְּמִינָא דְּקוֹמֶץ הוּא – לָא.
phrases.english: but this, which is not the same kind as the handful, does not count.
phrases.notes: "This" is the oil soaked into the wood from רבא's question in step 9.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, וְתִיבְּעֵי לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבינא's suggestion (step 10) that the bone dispute (steps 11-12) answers רבא's question.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the bone case and the oil case, starting with רבי יוחנן's side.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The bone is the same kind as the meat, but oil is not the same kind as the קומץ, so רבי יוחנן's reason may not apply.

steps.title: The question still stands for ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: Maybe even ריש לקיש only excludes the bone, because it can come apart from the meat. Oil cannot come apart from the קומץ, so it might count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe even ריש לקיש only said his rule about a bone, because a bone can come apart, and if it comes apart there is no מצוה to put it back on the fire. But oil, which cannot come apart, might count.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי finishes his rejection by showing that ריש לקיש's view also does not decide the oil case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש may say the bone does not count because it is really separate: if it falls off, nobody has to put it back. Oil soaked into the קומץ cannot be pulled out, so even ריש לקיש might count it as part of the קומץ. So neither side of the dispute settles רבא's question.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps
Something that can come apart and be separated
To put it back on the fire
Oil

phrases.english: Or perhaps, even according to Reish Lakish,
he only said his rule about a bone,
because it can come apart,
and if it comes apart, there is no מצוה to put it back,
phrases.notes: He means that if the bone falls off the fire, the כהן does not have to return it to the מזבח.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שֶׁמֶן דְּלָאו בַּר מִפְרַשׁ הוּא – לָא,
phrases.english: but oil, which cannot come apart, his rule does not apply to it,

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא, אֲפִילּוּ לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לָא קָא אָמַר אֶלָּא בְּעֶצֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב אשי's rejection from step 13, now from ריש לקיש's side.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the bone case and the oil case, now from ריש לקיש's side.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The bone can come apart from the meat, but the oil cannot come apart from the קומץ, so ריש לקיש's reason may not apply.

steps.title: Maybe there is no difference, so the question stays open
steps.stepSummary: The other side of the question: maybe the bone and the oil are the same after all. The גמרא cannot decide, so it ends with תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps there is no difference between the bone and the oil. The question stays unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the last possibility, that both cases are the same, and then ends the discussion with תיקו because it cannot decide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there is no difference, then each side would rule the same way on the oil as on the bone: רבי יוחנן would count the oil and ריש לקיש would not. Since we cannot tell whether the differences from steps 13-14 matter, רבא's question is left open.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no difference
The question stays unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's question about oil soaked into the wood is left as תיקו. The bone dispute does not answer it, because the bone and the oil may be different.

phrases.english: Or perhaps there is no difference.
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the last side of the question raised in steps 13-14 and closes the whole discussion of רבא's question.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We cannot tell whether oil soaked into the wood counts as part of the קומץ. The question stays תיקו.

steps.title: Two מנחות that got mixed before the קמיצה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if two מנחות got mixed before the קומץ was taken, they are fine if a קומץ can still be taken from each one separately. If not, they are פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two מנחות that did not yet have their קומץ taken got mixed with each other. If the כהן can take a קומץ from this one by itself and from that one by itself, they are כשר. If not, they are פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches what happens when two מנחות get mixed before their קומץ was taken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key question is whether each מנחה can still have its own קומץ taken from it alone. If the כהן can still reach a part that belongs only to one מנחה, both are fine. If they are fully mixed, both are פסול, because a קומץ cannot be taken from each one alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Had their קומץ taken
Got mixed together
Fit to be offered
Unfit, cannot be offered

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new topic, mixtures of whole מנחות, which follows the earlier discussion of mixing one item into another.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
Two meal offerings from which a handful was not yet taken
and they got mixed with each other,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יָכוֹל לִקְמוֹץ מִזּוֹ בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ
phrases.english: if he can take a handful from this one by itself
and from that one by itself, they are fit,
and if not, they are unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתֵּי מְנָחוֹת שֶׁלֹּא נִקְמְצוּ וְנִתְעָרְבוּ זוֹ בָּזוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ended with תיקו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mixed מנחות whose קומץ was not yet taken are כשר only if a קומץ can be taken from each one separately. Otherwise they are פסול.

steps.title: A handful mixed into a meal offering whose handful was never taken
steps.stepSummary: If a קומץ got mixed into a different מנחה that was never קמוץ, the כהן should not burn the mixture. If he did burn it, only the מנחה whose קומץ was taken counts for its owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: A קומץ got mixed into a מנחה that was not yet קמוץ. Do not burn it. If he burned it, the one that was קמוץ counts for the owner. The one that was not קמוץ does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of mixture cases. Here a ready קומץ fell into a whole מנחה that never had its קומץ taken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the first מנחה, its real קומץ did go up on the מזבח, so it works. The second מנחה never had a proper קומץ taken from it, so burning it all together does not count as its קמיצה. That is why only one owner is covered.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful of flour the כהן takes from a מנחה to burn on the מזבח
A meal offering made of flour
He should not burn it (on the מזבח), at the start
It counts for the owner; his obligation is fulfilled

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think both offerings are ruined, or that both are fine. The result splits: one owner is covered and the other is not.

phrases.english: A handful that got mixed
into a meal offering from which a handful was not taken
he should not burn it
but if he did burn it
this one, whose handful was taken, counts for the owner
phrases.notes: "This one" is the מנחה the קומץ came from.

phrases.english: and this one, whose handful was not taken
does not count for the owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of mixed-מנחה cases begun in step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not burn at the start. After the fact, the מנחה that was קמוץ counts and the one that was not קמוץ does not.

steps.title: A handful mixed back into leftovers
steps.stepSummary: If a קומץ got mixed into its own leftovers or into another מנחה's leftovers, the כהן should not burn it. If he did, the offering counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the קומץ got mixed into its own leftovers, or into the leftovers of another מנחה, do not burn it. If he burned it, it counts for the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its last mixture case. The קומץ was already taken, then fell back into leftover flour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the קומץ was properly taken, and it did go up on the מזבח, even though extra leftover flour went up with it. At the start we avoid burning leftovers on the מזבח. After the fact, the offering still works.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftovers of the מנחה after the קומץ is taken; the כהנים eat them
Its fellow, another מנחה

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's pattern: at the start, never burn a mixture. After the fact, an offering counts if its own proper קומץ went up.

phrases.english: If its handful got mixed into its own leftovers
or into the leftovers of another meal offering
he should not burn it
but if he did burn it, it counts for the owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final case in the same משנה; contrasts with step 17, where the other מנחה never had its קומץ taken
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קומץ mixed with leftovers should not be burned at the start, but if burned, the offering counts.

steps.title: Carcass meat is cancelled in slaughtered meat
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that a minority of נבילה mixed into שחוטה is cancelled, because שחוטה can never become נבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: נבילה gets cancelled in שחוטה, because slaughtered meat can never turn into נבילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a general rule from רב חסדא about mixtures and בטול. It will use this rule to look at mixtures like the ones in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's rule assumes that something mixed into its own kind is not cancelled, but something mixed into a different kind can be. He gives a test for whether two things count as different kinds: can the larger part ever become like the smaller part? Slaughtered meat can never become נבילה, so the two are treated as different kinds, and the נבילה is cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה; its meat makes people טמא
An animal that was properly slaughtered
Cancelled; it loses its own identity in the mixture
It is impossible

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a test for "same kind or different kind" that does not depend on what the food looks like. It depends on whether one can turn into the other.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Ḥisda says:
Carcass meat is cancelled in slaughtered meat
because it is impossible for slaughtered meat
to become carcass meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא נְבֵילָה בְּטֵילָה בִּשְׁחוּטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins after the משנה with a general rule about mixtures
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A minority of נבילה is cancelled in שחוטה, since שחוטה can never become נבילה.

steps.title: Slaughtered meat is not cancelled in carcass meat
steps.stepSummary: The other side of רב חסדא's rule: a minority of שחוטה is not cancelled in נבילה. A נבילה can lose its טומאה when it rots, so it can become like שחוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Slaughtered meat is not cancelled in נבילה, because נבילה can become like שחוטה. Once it rots, its טומאה flies away.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא finishes his rule by giving the reverse case, which comes out the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rotting נבילה stops being טמא, so in טומאה terms it can turn into something like שחוטה. Because one can become the other, they count as the same kind here. So the שחוטה is not cancelled. The direction of the change is what decides the result.

keyTerms.meaning: It rots, so badly that it is no longer fit to eat
Its טומאה flies away; it is no longer טמא

steps.confusionAlert: "Becomes שחוטה" does not mean the נבילה becomes kosher to eat. It only means it stops making things טמא, like slaughtered meat.
steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's rule works one way only. נבילה is cancelled in שחוטה, but שחוטה is not cancelled in נבילה, because only נבילה can change into the other.

phrases.english: But slaughtered meat is not cancelled in carcass meat
because it is possible for carcass meat
to become like slaughtered meat
phrases.notes: He means it can become like slaughtered meat in one way: it stops being טמא.

phrases.english: since when it rots
its impurity flies away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of רב חסדא's statement; the reverse case of step 19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A minority of שחוטה is not cancelled in נבילה, since נבילה can lose its טומאה by rotting and become like שחוטה.

steps.title: רבי חנינא gives the opposite rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says that anything able to become like the majority is not cancelled, and anything unable to become like it is cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא says: whatever can become like the other thing is not cancelled, and whatever cannot become like it is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא, רבי חנינא, gives his own rule for mixtures. It is the reverse of רב חסדא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא looked at whether the majority can become like the minority. רבי חנינא looks at whether the minority can become like the majority. So for him a little נבילה in a lot of שחוטה is not cancelled, because נבילה can rot and become like שחוטה. A little שחוטה in a lot of נבילה is cancelled, because שחוטה can never become נבילה.

keyTerms.meaning: it is able to become like it (the other item in the mixture)
cancelled, nullified in the majority
is not cancelled; keeps its own status

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא and רבי חנינא use the same idea, 'can it become like the other?', but they apply it in opposite directions. So their rulings come out reversed.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ḥanina says:
anything that is able to become like it
phrases.notes: He means the small amount, and whether it can become like the bigger amount it got mixed into.

phrases.english: is not cancelled,
and anything that is not able
to become like it is cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite opinion to רב חסדא's rule from steps 19-20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the minority can become like the majority, it is not cancelled. If it cannot, it is cancelled.

steps.title: Whose opinion do they follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which earlier opinion רב חסדא and רבי חנינא are following.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which earlier view the two אמוראים are basing themselves on. This question sets up the next moves, where each option will be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אמוראים say that in at least one direction a same-kind mixture is not cancelled. The גמרא wants to know which known opinion fits that idea.

keyTerms.meaning: according to (someone's opinion)
of whom

phrases.english: According to whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the basis of the two opinions in steps 19-21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which earlier opinion, the רבנן or רבי יהודה, do רב חסדא and רבי חנינא follow?

steps.title: It cannot follow the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: According to the רבנן, same kind with same kind is always cancelled, except for items that go on the מזבח. So neither אמורא's rule fits them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it follows the רבנן, they say that only items that go up on the altar do not cancel each other, but same kind with same kind is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option, the רבנן, and shows it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן hold that only things brought on the מזבח don't cancel each other. Otherwise, a same-kind mixture is simply cancelled by the majority. Meat of נבילה and meat of שחוטה are the same kind, so for the רבנן the minority should be cancelled in both directions. That clashes with both אמוראים.

keyTerms.meaning: items that go up on the מזבח
cancel each other out
a substance mixed with the same kind of substance

phrases.english: If it is according to the Rabbis,
but they say:
it is items that go up on the altar that do not cancel each other,
but same kind with same kind is cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רב חסדא and רבי חנינא follow the רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For the רבנן, a same-kind mixture is cancelled unless it is made of items that go on the מזבח. So שחוטה and נבילה should cancel each other in both directions, which leaves no room for a one-way rule.

steps.title: Starting to test רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to ask whether the two אמוראים follow רבי יהודה, and opens a challenge to that idea too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it follows רבי יהודה, but surely...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second option, רבי יהודה, and starts a challenge with 'but surely'. The challenge itself continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that same kind with same kind is not cancelled. That would mean nothing is cancelled in either direction, which also doesn't match a one-way rule. The full wording of the challenge comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: if (opening one possible option)
but surely (opening a challenge)

phrases.english: If it is according to Rabbi Yehuda,
but surely...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the רבנן (step 23) to the second option, רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רב חסדא and רבי חנינא follow רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה holds that same kind with same kind is not cancelled at all, which seems to rule out a one-way rule. The full challenge continues on the next עמוד.
